newsitem.title: USA: Staples, Office Depot agree to sell 63 stores competitor.
newsitem.headline: Staples, Office Depot agree to sell 63 stores competitor.

text.p: Office Max Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy 63 stores from competitors Staples Inc. and Office Depot if the Federal Trade Commission will drop its objection to the $4 billion acquisition of Staples by Office Depot.
Office Max, which currently operates 575 stores, said it agreed to pay $109 million for the stores.

The agreement was reached two days after the FTC voted to seek a court injunction to prevent the acquisition of Staples by Office Depot, fearing that the merger would cause price increases for consumers by reducing competition among office supply superstores.
Staples and Office Depot agreed to sell stores located primarily in the Southeastern states and in southern California.
Office Max said it currently does not have stores in those locations.
Office Max, Office Depot and Staples are the only office superstore chains in the United States.
